Asked for API 5 and no more, and named the client chat.progressive.client

The signature inside the archive is what anything below 7.0 reads, so
below 24 it is made again.

draw the text: Open Sans shipped in the binary; two ABIs built; APKs named by commit

A build in a browser has no system whose fonts it could ask: without the
faces a program ships itself, skiff draws the plates, the rows and the
bubbles and no word in any of them -- which is what the page has been
showing. Open Sans, regular and semibold (SIL Open Font License 1.1), is
therefore embedded and named as the program's faces, so that text is drawn
in a browser and is the same one on every other machine.

The android job builds 32-bit ARM beside 64-bit now, each on its own, and
an APK taken out of the archive says which commit it came from in its own
name.

android: say the ABI's own concurrency group where the ABI is known

The matrix that names each ABI is not read at the workflow's top level --
where it was, the file did not start a build at all. Each job says its own
group now.

keep Open Sans's own license file under its own name

Its text is kept as it was written: not the one extension the check reads
the license out of, so that no line need be added to it.

give the app progressive-chat's own icon: adaptive since 26, plates since 5

The launcher has been showing Android's own default figure for want of any
other. What it shows instead is the bubble with what grows in it, as
progressive-chat/progressive-android ships it: a plate and a figure apart
for the launches that cut one out of both, and one plate of each size for
what is older than that.

The resources are compiled one file at a time and linked beside the
manifest now -- which they were not before, this build having had no
resource of its own to link -- and the page shows the same figure.

say again that a part sized in pixels is sized in pixels, not in shares

A part made once to fill its column keeps saying so: what it is given
later is a width in pixels, and a part that still says it fills is read
as asking for that many columns -- 1040 of them, which is what the
window is wide beside the drawer. So the messages, their bar and the
card under them were laid out a million pixels across, and everything
said in them stood off the window: the plates stayed where they were
painted, and nothing written was.

Every size given again from the window's own size now says what it is:
not of the parent, of itself.

say in the readme why this is here, and what it is for now

It began as a client for people and stopped; it is a client for a model
now, on the stack of the one found asking a model what had been written
since.

begin what is said below the band, not under it

The bar over the messages is not a bar but a band of the paper's own
colour, and it reaches a hundred and eighty points down: what was said
first began at two and fifty, and so stood in the thick of it -- a
colour over the words, which is why the bubbles looked empty. What the
column is padded by at its top is now the band's own height: the words
begin where the band has faded out, and only go under it when the
column has moved them there.

say the toolchain's own sources for 32-bit arm, not only for 64

The tool that makes the toolchain is given one manifest, and its own
names one architecture in it: aarch64. So what was built for the
32-bit line was a 64-bit library, and the packaging of it said so --
the same sources, said the way 32-bit ARM spells them: the triple the
compiler is given, the triple the sysroot's directories have, the
name the ABI goes by in an APK, and neon, which Clang 23 will not
assume by itself.

keep the conversation mux was found in

What turned up that day is worth keeping as it was written down: the
export of the conversation, unedited, and a line in the README's own
story pointing at it -- so that 'found in a conversation with a model'
is not only said here, but can be read through to.

the bubble is its own colour, not a plate behind its words

A bubble's plate had to be put out of the flow of the lines it is
behind: only so is it as big as they come to without being one of the
things measured. Out of the flow is over it, to a browser -- what is
out of the flow is drawn above what is still in it -- so the plate's
colour was a colour over the words, and the bubbles read as empty.
The bubble's own colour and corners are its own, now: nothing between
a line and what is behind it.

one abi: 64-bit arm, and only it

It was tried the other way, and 32-bit ARM does not come out of it:
the platform's own kernel headers have a field of a type this clang
has no name for below 64 bits, so the compiler's own builtins -- the
first thing built, before there is a libc++ or a library of ours --
do not compile. Nothing of ours is in that failure, and nothing of
ours could be patched around it that would be worth keeping. So: the
one ABI every phone of the last years has, built, rather than two of
which one would only ever be red.

32-bit arm again: its own kernel headers, from its own directory of bionic

How it was found failing was in the compiler's own builtins, before
there is a libc++ or a library of ours: asm/sigcontext.h with a field
of __uint128_t in it, which this clang has no name for below 64 bits.
Not a header of ours to patch, then, but the wrong headers: bionic
keeps one architecture's asm headers, and the tool that makes the
toolchain names asm-arm64 -- so this adds what needed adding, which
is nothing about our sources and everything about which directory the
headers come from.

The target is said too, as before: armv7a as Clang spells it,
arm-linux-androideabi as the sysroot's own directories do, neon and
-mthumb, which are not assumed for 32-bit ARM. Two ABIs, two APKs --
and the 32-bit line's cache under another name, because what it had
kept was made of the wrong architecture's headers.

32-bit arm: the release these headers come from

The second thing only 32-bit ARM could not build was Android's own:
AHardwareBuffer's usage flags are an enum, and android-14 spells one
of them 1UL << 32 -- which is no constant expression at all where long
is 32 bits wide. Skia's hardware buffers, SDL's activity and this
program's own entry all include the header, so nothing of 32-bit ARM
got past it.

Android fixed that shifting in a later release (1ULL), so the release
every source is resolved through is said again here: android-16, for
64-bit ARM too, since a toolchain is one set of headers and it should
not be two.

32-bit arm: the one shift in android's own headers

Taking the later release whole was the cleaner of the two ways, and it
does not go: 16's framework resources are compiled against aapt2 too
old to read a configuration of 'de-feminine' and the rest of the
grammatical inflections it added, and the toolchain is not made at
all -- not for one ABI, for both.

So the release stays, and what is taken from the later one is the line
that keeps 32-bit ARM from being built: AHardwareBuffer's front-buffer
usage, written 1UL << 32, which is no constant expression where long
is 32 bits. Android wrote 1ULL there in a later release; this writes
it too, in the sysroot the toolchain has just made, for both ABIs --
a toolchain is one set of headers, not two.

the readme: one installable per abi, not one

A 32-bit ARM APK comes out of the same build now, so what the newest
android run publishes is two artifacts, each with the commit in its
name.

what an android has to be asked for: 21, not 5

The APK said minSdkVersion 5 -- a release of 2009 -- and an Android of
this decade answers it with "there was a problem while parsing the
package". Asked for 21 now, and aimed at 35, which is what mux asks
for and aims at: 21 is honest here, because nothing later than 21 is
what the libraries actually ask for -- no symbol of a later release is
left undefined in them, which is read out of them, not assumed.

And what installs is put up on its own: an artifact keeping the signed
APK, the unsigned one and the symbols all together is three files to
choose from, and the wrong one of the three is refused too.

the design asked for, drawn: bubbles, answers, and what they are asked for

What the reader wrote is a bubble on the right -- three quarters of the
room its widest -- with the corner at its bottom right squarer than the
three it turns away, and nothing over it: what says whose it is is where
it stands, which is one of the two ways asked for.

What a model answered is no bubble at all: text the whole breadth of the
room, no name over it and no model. Above it, folded, how long it was
thinking and how many tool calls it made, and pressed open, what it wrote
to itself while it was -- in green. At its foot six things: copy, again,
fork, share, info, delete.

What is written in now says which model answers in this chat and draws a
ring for how full its window is; the top of the messages has what makes a
chat new, and beside it what this one has been worth in tokens.

Every number shown is made up by the sample, which is not the program:
nothing of a protocol is here yet to read them out of.

what an answer can be asked for, answered again

The six taken into the visitor were written into a comment by mistake, so
what an answer is asked for at its foot had no one to answer it and
nothing in the program could be built at all. Written in again, one after
the other, and each saying what it does with the answer: taken whole,
thought again with everything after it put away, taken into a chat of its
own, given away as it reads, or rubbed out.

what an android is given is named for what it is first

progressive-chat-0.1-515bdffbe9d2-arm64-v8a.apk, and not
progressive-chat-arm64-v8a-515bdffbe9d2.apk: what the archive around it
is called, and what it holds, are now the same three things in the same
order -- which program, which commit, which machine -- instead of the one
beginning where the other ends. Two builds of one version sort by their
commit; two of one commit sort by their machine.

built as a release, so that an activity has time to load it in

What an Android opened was built without optimization, with Skia's and
HarfBuzz's own checking left in it: everything the first frame needs --
every word shaped, every glyph drawn -- was done at that size, while the
screen stayed black. mux loads faster because it is not built this way.

A release build with nothing asked of the debugger: -O2 and -g0, as the
page is built for the browser already.

what the deployed page paints, shot by a browser driven once

Asked for by hand and never by a push: a browser is minutes of its own
here, and the page it shot is the page a push has not yet replaced. So
that a report that the design is not to be seen can be answered from what
a window shows -- how many nodes the tree has, what they say, and both a
window's and a phone's breadth of the same page.

the probe asks for no GPU, and says what it saw before anything went

A renderer that asks a runner for what it has not got goes rather than
draws, and everything asked of the page afterwards is asked of nothing.
So Chromium is told to draw the way a runner can, and what the tree says
is printed before the picture is taken, so that a page that goes still
leaves an answer behind.

the probe asks a page of one thread too, and says when the renderer went

Whether a page was isolated -- and so whether the client drew it on one
thread or more -- is half of what such a report leaves out; so a context
that blocks the worker is asked as well, and going is said where going
happens rather than afterwards as an error of its own.

the probe draws in one process, so that what it draws it draws at all

A renderer of its own was going before the client had said it started,
which is going too early to have been the client's doing. One process,
no GPU, and as much room as a runner has: what is left after that is
either a page that draws or a page that never could have.

what version this is said with its commit, built as mux builds, and what is still wrong

The version was 0.1 and nothing else: a hundred builds share it, and none
of them can be told apart where it is said -- an Android's own list of
programs, and now the foot of the settings page too. So it is said as its
number and the commit it was built of, once in CMake, and it is what the
APK is given for its version name.

Built as mux builds it, which is why mux loaded faster even without a
release: Debug was asked for and Debug got -- with none of what a release
optimizes -- and the first frame asked all of Skia and HarfBuzz at that
size while the screen was still black. Now Debug, and -O3 over it.

And written down what is known wrong, the icon first, so that none of it
is only remembered between builds.

the page says which build it is while it starts

Starting progressive-chat... and nothing else answers nothing when the
page never stops starting, or when two of them are open side by side and
only one of them is the new one. build.json is given the version said in
CMake -- the number and the commit -- and what the page says as it starts
says it too.

an android asks nothing of a push that changed nothing in an android

Half a line of its own for a task, a note of what is still wrong, a page
saying which build it is: none of them is in the APK, and each of them
cost three quarters of an hour of each machine, made only to be put out
again by hand -- which is why builds of yours kept going grey. Now only
what an APK is made of asks either line to build one.

every build keeps its full BMI, so a release build is not a different program

What a release build was asked for was a reduced BMI, and a reduced BMI
leaves out the definition of a function that is not inline -- among them
every one whose type is deduced, which a view's is. Built that way the
program went as soon as it started.

Kept in every build instead, as mux keeps it by never asking for a
release at all: Debug it asks for, and -O3 over Debug, which is what we
ask now too.

git asked for as a program, so asking it does not load cmake-everywhere's list first

The port that is asked for first is the port that is used, and
cmake-everywhere answers every find_package by loading what it knows,
which is its own sdl3 before this project's. One find_package(Git) put
there to say what commit a build was made of made every android build
ask for a released SDL 3.4.16 -- one with no SDL3/SDL_nativeactivity.h
in it, and so no activity to start.

Asked as a program instead: nothing answers a program, and the fork with
the entry point is what is asked for again.

the icon progressive-android keeps, in every density and both shapes

A hand of ours had drawn a bubble for it, and it was not the icon of
this program: progressive-android keeps one picture, 512x512, its own
green to all four sides. What an Android asks a program for is made of
that one picture now -- five densities of the plate, five of the round
plate for a launcher that cuts a circle, and five of an adaptive icon's
foreground, its picture held inside the 66dp a plate of any shape is
sure to keep.

Made by tools/make_icons.py rather than kept by hand, and the colour an
adaptive icon is drawn on is read out of the picture's own rim, so a
plate cut through it shows no edge.

And written down that the program goes as soon as it starts, on an
android and in a browser both, with a workflow that runs it under the
sanitizers so that where it goes is said at last instead of guessed at.

what the APK is linked of is named after the icon, not before it

The icon was one vector of a bubble, and is five pictures cut from one
512x512 picture now: the file the APK's list named for its foreground
went with it, and both lines stopped at a name for something that was
not there.

Named for what is there, and for every plate too -- the round one was
never named by it, though aapt2 has always had it -- and the picture
everything is cut from moved out of the resource tree, which is not
where a source belongs.

the sanitizers' runtime is not in the clang this build asks for

clang 23 out of apt.llvm.org comes without libclang_rt.asan.a, and a
configure asking for it never got past asking whether the compiler
works at all. Asked for here, with the build that wants it, so that no
other build pays for it.

And it runs in a window of its own now rather than in none: SDL's dummy
driver has no GL behind it, and what is being looked for is what
happens when there is one.

a window is not built on what little stack there is

Thirty-two rows, each a tree of its own of thirty or so nodes, were kept
as a member of the screen that holds them -- made where the screen was
made and moved where it was moved to, and a megabyte is what an android
gives a thread and what this page asks for. Both went before anything
was drawn, every time, saying nothing.

The rows are made on the heap now, and what is left of the screen is
asked of a stack again. Insurance besides it, since asking for a little
and meaning to grow is not asking for enough: sixteen megabytes for the
thread the program is run on in an APK, four for the browser's.

a GL that answers, before a window that asks it

What the program asked of GL in the last run it asked of nothing: no X
server had been started and SDL had been left its dummy driver, which
has no GL behind it at all. Skia asks GL what it knows, is given a
pointer that is nothing, and goes inside its own answer -- which says
what that machine was rather than what this program is.

Mesa in software now, and an X server in front of it, so that what this
program asks of a window is asked of one that is really there.
where it stands is read before what it is made of

what is still to be done, said again, and committing through the account that made it

tools/commit.py: what is changed here, given to GitHub as one commit of
its own, so that it is written down as MaurerAnton and not as an address
no account answers to. Twice over it went wrong before this and is said
here because of it: base_tree beside the tree rather than in the same
body as it is not given at all, and what comes of that is a commit of
nothing but the files named, all the others taken away -- so it counts
the files now, before anything moves, and moves nothing when the count
is wrong.

And written down where the program goes on a desktop: inside Skia,
asking GL what it knows, given a pointer that is nothing.

client.wasm was never meant to be kept: it is what building the page
leaves in the root, and it is not part of anything.

the probe asks for a GL, and not for none of it

SwiftShader instead of --disable-gpu: what the client draws through is
WebGL, and Chromium told there is no GPU to ask has none, so it went
inside Skia asking GL what it knows -- which is where this same program
goes on a desktop with no window behind it, and says of the machine it
ran on rather than of the page.

It asks what WebGL it got now, and says it, so that a page that does not
paint can be told apart from a browser that cannot paint anything.

the page paints now, and what still does not is the phone

The probe's own browser had been told --disable-gpu, which is told to
have no WebGL at all: so it went inside Skia asking GL what it knows,
and was reported as the page going. Asked for SwiftShader instead, it
paints -- 1532 nodes, the whole of the design read off it.

Written down too that Skia asking GL what it knows is given nothing is
one going with three faces, desktop and browser alike, and that whether
the phone is the third has still not been said.

And the narrow page: 390x844 with the worker blocked does not start, and
nobody has looked at it yet.

the APK says where it went, so that the phone need not be asked

`adb logcat -d -s progressive-chat`: what made it go, and where. Asked
for as soon as the library is started, and said before the signal is
raised again as it would have been -- so Android's own tombstone, with
its trace of the frames, comes after it.

It says that it started too: `starting on a thread of 16777216 bytes`,
or that it could not have one and is running on SDL's. Either way the
answer is in a log and not in somebody's memory of a screen that went
black.

And what the tool left behind it: reset --soft moves what git thinks
HEAD is and not what it thinks is staged, so every commit made through
GitHub showed the one before it as still undone. --mixed now.

two headers the 32-bit build asked for

<initializer_list> for the list of signals this file asks to be told of,
and <cstddef> for what it asks the thread's stack to be: neither came
with anything else it includes, and armeabi-v7a said so -- which is why
it is built for both as one library and not only where it is tested.

what the switches ask for, answered; the search's own rows

Four rows of the Settings page were drawn and did nothing: the seeds,
the larger type, the pure black, and a font no build can load. A press
now asks for one whole thing -- which seed grows every colour, whether
the body is set larger, which way the light goes -- and the program
grows the looks again before the next frame. The fourth row asked for a
font that nothing here can set, so it is a light switch instead, which
is a thing the colours can actually be.

The drawer searched and showed everything regardless: the rows it keeps
now are the ones the search kept. Its foot opens Settings, and the page
put away again by its own corner. The top bar kept a magnifier that was
never wired to anything, so it is gone: searching is the drawer's to do.
What answered in a chat is said where About asks about it, next to the
tool calls and the tokens. Two roles no part read, and two ternaries
asking a question they already knew the answer to, are gone from theme.

a theme the requests are written in, which they were not

The seeds a row asks for are named by pchat.theme, and the file that
says what a request is did not ask for that module, so the build did not
get as far as the window. It imports it now.

the clock asks for the model it reads a moment out of

clock_of moved into ui:base so that a drawer's row and a message's foot
say the hour the same way, and base -- which never had a moment in it --
did not import the module the moment is written in.

two colours of a search that is no longer there

The magnifier went out of the bar but two lines still set its colours.

what is written on the wire, read once and written again

A brace does not belong to any screen. What comes off a provider -- and what
is kept on the disk, later -- is text, and it is read here into values of its
own: a thing, a list, a number, a truth, a string, or nothing. A reader says
where it gave up, so that a bad answer can be said as a bad one at its own
place in it, and a writer keeps its commas itself, so that nothing building a
body has to count them.

Nothing else in the program reads this text: it is the only place braces are
looked at, and it says nothing about any protocol on top of them.

what is asked of a model, and what its stream says coming back

The client had nothing a provider could be spoken to through. This is that
seam, and only that seam: one module writes the body a chat wire asks for --
the turns of a conversation, what the model is told, that it streams and that
it says what the stream cost -- and another reads the stream it answers with,
one frame at a time, into text, what it thought, the tools it asked for and
what it cost.

No socket in either. feed() takes bytes in whatever sizes they come in, so a
transport is only a thing that hands bytes over: Emscripten's fetch on the
web, a socket on the desk, later Asio on fibers as mux does. Both halves are
said by tests, and said twice -- whole, and cut three characters at a time,
because a wire does not cut where it is convenient to read.

tools/commit.py said a new directory as a directory, and GitHub asked for the
files in it; it says every file of one now.

every test asked for by one name, so that a new one is run too

The check said the three tests it knew by name, and ctest counted five --
two of which nothing had built. Every test added here is added to one
target now, and the check asks for the target.

a value cannot be written out in full inside itself

A thing's members were a list of pairs, and a pair will not hold a type it
does not yet know in full -- so the members are members now, written after
the value is, and the two containers a value holds are held through a
pointer, which is the only way it says "a list" without already being one.
two whole numbers said as the doubles they are, so that no call is two calls

every variant here is splice's now, as every variant in mux is

What the family shares was here only as skiff's own ask for it, taken from
skiff's pin and not from the pin this build says. Said first now, before
skiff asks, in the version mux says: spl::variant where a value or a request
was a std::variant of kinds, and spl::overloaded to read it, so that every
alternative is handled and a new one cannot be forgotten -- which is what a
get_if chain let a new alternative be.

Nothing else of splice is taken. And what a conversation's turns are given
as is any range of messages now, and not one vector of one type.

one answer, from what is asked of it to the message it leaves

A body written for a wire and a stream read out of one were two halves with
nothing between them: who would have held what had come so far, what it
cost, what stopped it, and whose it was to say it was over? This is what
holds one answer while it arrives, and only that -- no socket in it, no
call made into anything: what is to be carried is written out for whoever
carries it, as data, and what comes back is handed to it, as data, and it
says when nothing more is coming.

So a page's fetch, a socket or a fiber can carry it without any of this
knowing which, and a test carries it whole with no network under it at all.

What it leaves is a message as the model keeps one: what the model answered,
what it thought before it spoke, how many tools it asked for, what it cost,
and failed where nothing of it came to be read.

core::thought said in full, for thought here is what it thought

Inside the class, thought is the answer's own word for what was thought
before it spoke, and not the type that word is kept in.

the type that thought is kept in, said from outside the class

Inside a class whose own word for what an answer thought is thought, the
type pchat::thought has to be said from outside it.

the page asks the server that served it, and an answer is written as it comes

Two halves with nothing between them: a model could be asked and an answer
could be read out of a stream, but nothing carried one to the other, and no
screen had ever seen an answer arrive. So there is what hands a body over
and takes bytes back -- on a page, through the browser's own fetch, streamed
